key_insight: By concatenating GKP and Steane error correction in an all-photonic repeater, the paper achieves 1,000 km quantum communication with 9 km repeater spacing while improving robustness to photon loss.
engineering_relevance: The design reduces the resource burden of long-distance quantum networking by using a free-space photonic memory cavity, improved Bell-pair construction heuristics, and realistic error modeling.
method: Use concatenated bosonic GKP + discrete-variable [[7,1,3]] Steane codes to protect elementary Bell pairs.
Introduce a multi-reflection mirror-based optical cavity as a free-space photonic memory module.
Compare two Bell-pair construction heuristics: one more resource-intensive but limited to two-qubit correlated errors, the other cheaper but tolerating up to three-qubit correlated errors.
evidence_signal: Simulation results under optical and switching-induced imperfections indicate only a few thousand GKP qubits per repeater station per protocol run, substantially below prior third-generation all-photonic repeater resource demands.
watch_item: The architecture depends on practical performance of the optical cavity, switching, and high-fidelity GKP-state preparation, which may be difficult to realize experimentally.
paper_title: High-Rate and Resource-Efficient All-Photonic Quantum Repeater Architectures with 9 km Repeater Spacing
